The '''2010–11 Czech First League''' season, known as the [[Gambrinus (beer)|Gambrinus]] liga for sponsorship reasons, was the 18th edition of the top flight [[Czech First League]] annual [[Association football|football]] tournament. It began on 16 July 2010 and finished on 28 May 2011. [[AC Sparta Prague|Sparta Prague]] were the [[2009–10 Czech First League|2010 champions]], their 11th Czech Republic championship.

==Teams==
[[FK Bohemians Praha (Střížkov)|FK Bohemians]] and [[SK Kladno]] were relegated to the [[2010–11 Czech 2. Liga]] after finishing last and second to last, respectively, in the [[2009–10 Czech First League|2009–10 season]]; Bohemians were denied a license to play professional football the following season and were thus further demoted to the [[Bohemian Football League]] (third division) in June 2010.<ref>{{Cite news|first=Jaromír|last=Novák|title=Střížkov první ligu zakončil v plusu, nový soutěžní ročník začne v ČFL|url=https://www.idnes.cz/fotbal/prvni-liga/strizkov-prvni-ligu-zakoncil-v-plusu-novy-soutezni-rocnik-zacne-v-cfl.A100625_112314_fotbal_mn|newspaper=Mladá fronta Dnes|publisher=Mafra|date=25 June 2010|access-date=25 January 2025|language=cs}}</ref> The relegated teams were replaced by [[2009–10 Czech 2. Liga|2009–10 2. Liga]] champions [[FC Hradec Králové]] and runners-up [[FK Ústí nad Labem]].{{Citation needed|date=January 2025}}

Furthermore, ''1. FC Brno'' was renamed [[FC Zbrojovka Brno]] effective to the beginning of this season.<ref>{{Cite news|first=Robin|last=Krutil|title=Staronový název přijde fotbalovou Zbrojovku na statisíce korun|url=https://www.idnes.cz/brno/zpravy/staronovy-nazev-prijde-fotbalovou-zbrojovku-na-statisice-korun.A100622_1405821_brno-zpravy_zma|newspaper=Mladá fronta Dnes|location=Brno|publisher=Mafra|date=26 June 2010|access-date=25 January 2025|language=cs}}</ref> Following trouble at their [[Czech Cup]] semi-final match, which was abandoned at half time and awarded 3–0 to the visiting team, [[SK Slavia Prague]] were fined 750,000 [[CZK]] and ordered to play three home games behind closed doors.<ref>{{Cite news|first=Aleš|last=Berný|title=Policie pátrá kvůli incidentu na fotbalové Slávii po dvaceti fanoušcích|url=http://praha.idnes.cz/policie-patra-kvuli-incidentu-na-fotbalove-slavii-po-dvaceti-fanouscich-1au-/praha-zpravy.aspx?c=A110513_150308_praha-zpravy_ab|newspaper=Mladá fronta Dnes|location=Prague|publisher=Mafra|date=13 May 2011|access-date=23 August 2011|language=cs}}</ref> Since there were only two home matches left in the season, one was suspended until the next season.<ref>{{Cite news|first=Petr|last=Šedivý|title=Slavia si odpykala trest: všechny zápasy bez diváků vyhrála|url=http://fotbal.idnes.cz/slavia-si-odpykala-trest-vsechny-zapasy-bez-divaku-vyhrala-p4p-/fotbal.aspx?c=A110815_070336_fotbal_pes|newspaper=Mladá fronta Dnes|location=Prague|publisher=Mafra|date=15 August 2011|access-date=23 August 2011|language=cs}}</ref>

*{{note|1|1}} Příbram coach Roman Nádvorník was sacked on 26 April 2011. Two members of staff at the club, David Vavruška and [[František Kopač]], were appointed to serve as caretaker managers until the end of the season.<ref name=pribramcaretakers>{{Cite news|first=Jaromír|last=Novák|title=V Příbrami už nového kouče nehledají, důvěru mají Kopač s Vavruškou|url=http://fotbal.idnes.cz/v-pribrami-uz-noveho-kouce-nehledaji-duveru-maji-kopac-s-vavruskou-1dn-/fotbal.aspx?c=A110428_135158_fotbal_mn|newspaper=Mladá fronta Dnes|publisher=Mafra|date=2 May 2011|access-date=2 August 2011|language=cs}}</ref> Exactly one month later, on 26 May, David Vavruška was appointed manager of the club on a permanent basis.
*{{note|2|2}} Mladá Boleslav appointed sporting director [[Ladislav Minář]] to the position of caretaker manager until the end of the season.<ref name=stannerout/> Following the end of the season, Miroslav Koubek took over.

==European competitions==
{{Unreferenced section|date=January 2025}}

=== 2010–11 UEFA Champions League===
[[AC Sparta Prague|Sparta Prague]] started in the [[2010–11 UEFA Champions League#Second qualifying round|second qualifying round]] of this season's Champions League. After defeating Latvian club [[FK Liepājas Metalurgs]] by a 5–0 aggregate scoreline, they qualified for the next round. Sparta defeated Polish club [[Lech Poznań]] in the third qualifying round, winning both matches by a score of 1–0. Losing 2–0 and 1–0 to Slovak club [[MŠK Žilina|Žilina]] in the play-off round ended Sparta's involvement in the competition for this season.

=== 2010–11 Europa League ===
[[FC Baník Ostrava|Baník Ostrava]] was the only Czech team involved in the [[2010–11 UEFA Europa League#Second qualifying round|second qualifying round]] of the Europa League. They got past Georgian club [[FC WIT Georgia|WIT Georgia]] with a goalless second leg result, having won the first match 6–0. In the third round, [[FC Viktoria Plzeň|Viktoria Plzeň]] and [[FK Jablonec|Jablonec]] also entered the competition. However, all three Czech teams lost: Baník Ostrava 3–1 on aggregate to Belarusian club [[FC Dnepr Mogilev|Dnepr Mogilev]]; Viktoria Plzeň and Jablonec 4–1 on aggregate, respectively to Turkish club [[Beşiktaş J.K.|Beşiktaş]] and Cypriot club [[APOEL F.C.|APOEL]].

Sparta Prague qualified for the group stage of the Europa League due to their performance in the Champions League. With results of two wins, three draws, and one loss, they finished second in Group F – behind [[CSKA Moscow]] (Russia) but ahead of [[Palermo FC|Palermo]] (Italy) and [[FC Lausanne-Sport|Lausanne-Sport]] (Switzerland). As a result, they advanced to the knockout phase of the competition. English club [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] provided the opposition after a goalless first game in Prague. A single goal from striker [[Dirk Kuyt]] eliminated Sparta from the Europa League, 1–0 in the match and on aggregate.
